goal: Extract a reusable engineering lesson from one valid failed language-to-graph interface experiment without entering a repair loop.
root_cause_hypothesis: The new specialist was query-and-relation-conditioned but not edge-content-conditioned. A one-edge/two-field factorial curriculum could reward a relation-global endpoint polarity without requiring the model to bind the query to a specific source/target pair. The same learned polarity then destructively tilted real mixed evidence graphs.
transferable_lessons: A causal curriculum must rule out the exact shortcut the architecture can exploit, not only obvious constant-label shortcuts.
When the parent decision function uses source and target content, a specialist that modifies that decision surface should normally observe the same edge context or be explicitly routed away.
Exact zero initialization protects only the initial state. It does not guarantee preservation after specialist training.
Use richer multi-edge counterfactuals before claiming query-to-graph binding.
Preserve failed artifacts and stop after a valid failure; change the abstraction only after architectural localization.
next_method_seed: Keep the proven graph read as a frozen shared expert. Build an edge-specific query cross-attention specialist that sees query tokens, relation, source state, and target state; emit independent gated source/target residuals. Qualify exact-parent behavior before any gradient decision.
